key_insight: Keeping only deltas resident works: a 70B FP16 base is 140 GB, and a 1-bit sign delta plus scales is ~9 GB, so N tenants cost ~1+N/16 copies.
killer_doubt: BitDelta already fuses 1-bit deltas into the GEMM, and LoRA adapters are ~0.1-1% of the base. Multi-tenant fine-tune hosting is a small slice of DRAM demand.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Reproduce BitDelta or S-LoRA/Punica serving 100 variants on one 8-GPU node and measure resident memory and tokens/s (<$20k).
prior_art: BitDelta (2024) fused 1-bit deltas; S-LoRA, Punica, dLoRA multi-adapter serving; DeltaZip compressed-delta serving. From memory.

key_insight: A 1024-d fp32 vector is 4 KB and its sign code is 128 B. Popcount Hamming search plus an NVMe rerank holds 32x more vectors per GB of DRAM.
killer_doubt: Every major vector DB already ships this. Reranking 100 candidates of 4 KB each caps one ~1M-IOPS SSD near 10k QPS, and vector search is under 1% of DRAM demand.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Benchmark existing binary quantization with rescoring (Qdrant, Weaviate, FAISS) on BEIR or MS MARCO, recall against DRAM per vector (<$10k).
prior_art: DiskANN/SPANN (PQ codes in DRAM, full vectors on SSD); Qdrant, Weaviate, Elasticsearch binary quantization with rescoring; Cohere binary embeddings. From memory.

key_insight: Duplicate of I-00308: the same sign-code Hamming search with a flash rerank. Its value is as stated there, 32x more resident vectors per GB of DRAM.
killer_doubt: Same prior art as I-00308. Embeddings not trained Matryoshka-style lose ~4-8% recall at 1 bit before rerank, which forces deeper rerank lists and more NVMe IOPS per query.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Run the same benchmark as I-00308 (<$10k).
prior_art: Same as I-00308: DiskANN/SPANN, binary quantization with rescoring in Qdrant, Weaviate and Elasticsearch. From memory.

key_insight: Scoring on coarse planes and fetching exact low planes only for the top-k keeps every token losslessly addressable, so long contexts never need eviction.
killer_doubt: The split caps HBM saving at 2x (8 of 16 bits); lossy FP8/INT4 KV already gives 2-4x. Fetching 256 tokens' low planes (~40 MB) at 64 GB/s costs ~0.6 ms/step.
decisive_experiment: vLLM trace study (<$20k): compare FP8-high-plane top-k with lossless refetch against KIVI/KVQuant INT4 and Quest at equal accuracy on RULER. Report HBM bytes and tier traffic per decode step.
prior_art: SpAtten (HPCA 2021) MSB-first progressive fetch; Quest, ShadowKV and InfiniGen top-k KV offload; KIVI and KVQuant low-bit KV. From memory.

key_insight: One bit-plane copy serves several precisions. Its MSB planes double as a speculative draft that shares weights, saving the 2-16 GB a separate draft model occupies.
killer_doubt: Any-Precision LLM already does this. Batches mix quality tiers, so one high-tier request in a 70B batch streams 35 GB of LSB planes per step, 0.55 s over CXL x16.
decisive_experiment: One GPU node (<$30k): serve a Llama-70B bit-plane copy that drafts from its own MSB planes. Measure acceptance rate, tokens/s and resident DRAM against Any-Precision LLM and a separate 8B draft.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024) single-copy bit-plane multi-precision; Matryoshka Quantization (2025) nested int8/4/2; QSpec (2024) quantized self-draft. From memory.

key_insight: Bit-plane-major tiles let precision change per decode step without overfetch. At batch 1 (phones, laptops), easy tokens could move ~4-6x fewer weight bits.
killer_doubt: Weights are shared across a batch. With 80% easy tokens, P(all 64 easy) = 0.8^64 ~ 6e-7, so datacenter batches always fetch every plane. Truncated 2-bit planes are badly lossy.
decisive_experiment: Batch-1 laptop study (<$20k): Llama-8B in bit-plane layout with a per-token plane predictor. Measure bits fetched, perplexity and tokens/s against a native 4-bit model with the same DRAM footprint.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024) bit-plane layout; Matryoshka Quantization (2025); bit-serial accelerators Stripes and Bit-Pragmatic. From memory.

key_insight: If session state really could be distilled to ~1 MB without losing quality, that compression would cut server KV residency directly. Parking it on clients is secondary.
killer_doubt: Even MLA KV is ~70 KB/token: 8k tokens is 560 MB, ~4 minutes of uplink at 20 Mb/s. Idle KV already moves to NVMe (DeepSeek, Mooncake), not DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Software study (<$50k): score gist or KV distillation at 0.5-2 MB per 8k-32k-token session on multi-turn benchmarks against full KV. If quality holds, use it server-side first.
prior_art: CacheGen (SIGCOMM 2024) compresses KV into bitstreams for network transfer; gist tokens (Mu 2023); Mooncake and LMCache SSD KV tiers. Client parking: none found.

key_insight: Embedding tables are Zipfian. A hot set of full rows plus hashed compositional rows for the tail compresses multi-TB tables 10-100x.
killer_doubt: CAFE (SIGMOD 2024) already does hot-row promotion over a hashed tail. Ads models resist it because ~0.1% AUC loss costs more than the DRAM saved, so tables stay huge.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Reproduce CAFE or QR embeddings on Criteo-1TB or Avazu and report AUC against memory (<$20k).
prior_art: QR trick (Shi, KDD 2020); hash embeddings (2017); DHE (KDD 2021); CAFE (SIGMOD 2024) hot/cold adaptive embeddings; ByteDance Monolith. From memory.

key_insight: Promotion already copies every survivor and knows its class layout. So type-aware columnar packing (pointer deltas, enum dictionaries) can beat page-level LZ4 with no extra copy pass.
killer_doubt: Old gen is hot in caches and services. A decoded-cache miss (~100-300 ns), re-encoding on field writes, and the existing 4-15% load-barrier tax together could erase the gain.
decisive_experiment: MMTk/OpenJDK prototype (~$300k, two engineers): columnar promotion for the top classes. Measure old-gen ratio, decoded-cache hit rate, throughput and p99 on DaCapo, Renaissance, Cassandra and a Go service, against zswap.
prior_art: Zippads (ASPLOS 2019) object-based compressed hierarchy (hardware); embedded-Java heap compression (OOPSLA 2003); V8 pointer compression. Columnar GC packing: none found.

key_insight: Page-scale codes make 1% raw BER usable: channel capacity needs ~8% parity and BCH ~23%. A compressed far tier becomes a home for weak dies and low-charge cells.
killer_doubt: Beyond N-62 (1e-4, line BCH), going from 3.7 to 2.3 sigma buys only ~1.6x less charge but costs microsecond page decode and 4 KB read-modify-write; VRT drift breaks fixed parity.
decisive_experiment: DRAM-Bender on 20 DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs: map BER against refresh interval (1-16 s) and temperature, and VRT stability over weeks. Run an FPGA compress-plus-BCH controller on real page traces (~$150k).
prior_art: COP (ISCA 2015) and Frugal ECC (SC 2015) compression-funded line ECC; CREAM (HPCA 2017); NAND LDPC controllers. Page-scale 1%-BER DRAM tier: none found.

key_insight: Llama-70B KV is ~320 KB/token, while one 256-d latent is 512 B. With MLA-style absorbed up-projection, scoring stays in latent space and the FLOP cost stays small.
killer_doubt: All 80 layers re-read the latent, so bandwidth falls only ~8x unless 64 MB stays on-chip. Retrofits (xKV, MiniCache) stall near 2-7x before accuracy drops.
decisive_experiment: Distil Llama-3.1-8B into one shared 512-d latent with ~2-5B tokens (~$100k of GPU time). Compare RULER/LongBench at 32-128k against the MHA2MLA per-layer retrofit and YOCO-style half-depth sharing.
prior_art: MLA (DeepSeek-V2, 2024); CLA (2024); YOCO (2024); LCKV (ACL 2024) single top-layer KV; MHA2MLA and xKV retrofits (2025). From memory.

key_insight: Correct diagnosis of MXT: compression latency is free only where a hop already costs ~200 ns, so CXL Type-3 expanders are the right host.
killer_doubt: Already commercial. AI-era data (BF16/FP8 weights, KV, activations) compresses losslessly only ~1.1-1.3x, so the capacity gain collapses exactly where DRAM demand grows.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed for the concept. To bound effective capacity per workload, dump pages from LLM serving and general servers and measure LZ4/zstd ratio distributions (<$20k).
prior_art: IBM MXT (2000); OCP hyperscale CXL tiered-memory expander with inline compression; ZeroPoint Technologies; Google zswap far memory. From memory.
